text:
kevin: Quick question — for the new auth flow, should our tokens carry org/project scope as token claims, or should they be opaque and resolved via an auth lookup? This affects routing policies, quotas, telemetry, and the console rollout UX.

kevin: TL;DR: embedding claims lets edge routers enforce quotas without a central hop; opaque tokens centralize decisioning but require a fast auth lookup. Want opinions.

sophie: @kevin can we do a hybrid? include minimal claims (org_id, proj_id, token_version) + server-side lookup for expanded policies.

ashley: Edge enforcement is tempting — avoids an extra RPC per request. Downside: more complexity for key rotation and revocation. If token contains claims, edge must validate signature and know JWKS rotation.

tyler: For service-account key exchange today we mint short-lived projected tokens at /v1/token/exchange. If projected token includes org/proj, then routers can act immediately. But revocation becomes TTL-dependent.

deploy-bot: deploy: auth-service/v2 canary scheduled at 03:30 UTC — heads up for routing tests.

kevin: Example claim idea:

```json
{
  "iss": "auth.redwood.ai",
  "sub": "svc_abc123",
  "org": "org_123",
  "proj": "proj_456",
  "ver": "token_v1",
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

kevin: With that, edge router can apply routing policy by org/proj, enforce per-project quotas, and tag telemetry.

ashley: But note: rollout pain. Old edge nodes won't know new claim semantics unless we version tokens. Also key rotation: every edge will need fresh JWKS cache.

sophie: For the Console UX I think we should expose a toggle: "Auth mode: Token claims (fast edge enforcement)" vs "Auth mode: Central lookup (single source)" and a migration window with metrics. We need these metrics: percent_edge_enforced, avg_auth_latency, and mismatch_rate (edge vs central).

tyler: Telemetry wise we should add tags: auth.method=(claims|lookup), token.version, token.issuer. Also emit a sample boolean auth.edge_enforced. That will help validate correctness during rollout.

kevin: Another open item: service-account exchange flow — should /v1/token/exchange return a token with org/proj embedded, or a signed "policy cookie" that routers understand but which isn't a direct JWT claim? Cookies might be opaque but verifiable.

ashley: I'd prefer a signed claim in the projected token plus an exchange log entry for audit. For revocation: short TTL (e.g., 5m) plus a best-effort blacklist propagation to edges. That balances latency and safety.

sophie: What about cross-org delegation (marketplace integrations)? If an agent from Org A acts on behalf of Org B, token claims must include delegation metadata and trust chain. That will complicate the edge parser.

tyler: Also remember signature validation cost at the edge: HSM-backed key ops are heavy. We should keep signature validation local with cached JWKS and a small in-memory keyset.

kevin: Concrete action items: 1) prototype token_claims v1 (kevin + ashley) — include ver field and short TTL; 2) telemetry tagging spec (tyler) — add auth.method and token.version; 3) Console flag + rollout plan doc (sophie) — include migration window + metrics dashboard. I'll open an RFC and link here.

ashley: :thumbsup: I'll add notes about blacklist propagation and TTL heuristics to the RFC.

sophie: I'll mock up the Console toggle and the dashboard panels.

kevin: Thanks folks — let's sync tomorrow in the auth sync.
